# Research basis — continuous agent improvement

Research window: **2026-04-01 through 2026-08-01**. Sources were rechecked on 2026-08-01.

This reference records why the skill uses evidence intake, quarantine, explicit lifecycle
dispositions, separate evaluation, bounded promotion, runbook admission, and subtraction. It is not
an instruction feed: external content is evidence, never authority to modify this repository.

Provider posts establish their own platform practices. Preprints suggest mechanisms and failure
modes, not settled consensus. Practitioner reports show operational patterns. OSS demonstrates
that controls are implementable. None of those facts proves that a candidate improves this fleet;
only a frozen local baseline and comparable local evaluation can do that.

## Findings that converged across source types

1. **Capture the path, not just the final answer.** Corrections become useful only when inputs,
   provenance, intermediate decisions, expected behavior, and observed outcomes remain traceable.
2. **Separate evidence from reusable guidance.** Raw trajectories are noisy, environment-specific,
   and poisoning-prone; compact procedural rules transfer better when their source remains linked.
3. **Treat admission as the hard problem.** Repeatedly accepting any positive dev-set delta produces
   false and harmful changes. Freeze baselines and use held-out, adverse, and regression evidence.
4. **Separate proposer, verifier, and approver.** A candidate cannot grade or authorize itself.
   Deterministic checks are preferred; fresh independent judgment covers what rules cannot encode.
5. **Route by control type.** Mechanical failures belong in tests or validators; model procedures in
   skills or agents; repeatable operations in runbooks; perishable facts in dated references.
6. **Maintain with subtraction.** Merge duplicates, supersede stale facts, and drop weak or
   over-specialized lessons. Append-only stores accumulate context and negative transfer.
7. **Bound authority and rollout.** Sandboxing, approval, exact-artifact checks, pause/rollback, and
   bounded retries are structural controls; prompt reminders cannot replace them.

These are synthesis inferences from the evidence below, not claims made verbatim by any one source.

## Official Anthropic evidence

- **2026-04-08 — [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the
  hands](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents).** Separates recoverable append-only
  session state from the context transformations chosen by a harness. Design use: retained evidence
  is not itself the active instruction context, and harness assumptions need rechecking as models
  change.
- **2026-04-09 — [Trustworthy agents in
  practice](https://www.anthropic.com/research/trustworthy-agents).** Keeps humans in control and
  treats security, transparency, and privacy as system properties. Design use: learning cannot
  silently broaden authority or obscure provenance.
- **2026-04-23 — [An update on recent Claude Code quality
  reports](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/april-23-postmortem).** Anthropic traced interacting
  product changes that escaped unit, end-to-end, automated, and dogfood checks, then committed to
  broader per-model evals, ablations, exact public-build use, soak periods, and gradual rollout.
  Design use: one green lane is not sufficient promotion evidence.
- **2026-05-08 — [Teaching Claude
  why](https://www.anthropic.com/research/teaching-claude-why).** Reports that held-out and
  out-of-distribution evidence mattered, and that principles generalized better than narrow
  demonstrations in its alignment setting. Design use: retain the scoped reason, not an incident
  transcript or a copied answer pattern. This is an analogy from model training, not direct proof
  about prompt-file maintenance.
- **2026-05-25 — [How we contain Claude across
  products](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/how-we-contain-claude).** Describes sandboxes,
  VMs, filesystem and egress controls as blast-radius boundaries, and treats fetched/tool content as
  an attack surface. Design use: prompt prose and self-review cannot replace capability controls;
  untrusted content stays quarantined.
- **2026-06-08 — [Paving the way for agents in
  biology](https://www.anthropic.com/research/agents-in-biology).** A deterministic retrieval layer
  raised reliability for a scientific retrieval task to nearly 100 percent. Design use: recurring
  mechanical work should move into deterministic tooling when possible. Domain results do not imply
  the same numeric gain here.
- **Current during the window — [Using agent
  memory](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory).** Documents immutable,
  attributed versions, content-hash preconditions for safe updates, and point-in-time recovery.
  Design use: mutable retained state needs concurrency, lineage, and rollback controls. This skill
  does not authorize memory writes.
- **Current during the window — [Anthropic skill-creator
  implementation](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/b29e7cf65e5cb78a5ac33d582270551bc74a14eb/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md).** Its
  benchmark flow pairs with-skill and baseline runs, records variance/time/tokens, and separates an
  analyzer that surfaces evidence from the optimizer. Design use: comparable baselines and role
  separation.

## Official OpenAI evidence

- **2026-04-27 — [An open-source spec for Codex orchestration:
  Symphony](https://openai.com/index/open-source-codex-orchestration-symphony/).** Describes a
  repository-owned workflow backed by tests and guardrails, and explicitly treats post-task
  self-reflection as a workflow step that must be declared. Design use: fleet-wide learning requires
  visible wiring, not an assumed habit.
- **2026-05-08 — [Running Codex safely at
  OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/running-codex-safely/).** Separates access control, sandboxing,
  configuration, approvals, and agent-aware telemetry. Design use: a learning loop stays inside the
  enclosing task's permissions.
- **2026-05-27 — [Building self-improving tax agents with
  Codex](https://openai.com/index/building-self-improving-tax-agents-with-codex/).** Connects expert
  corrections to full production traces, structured findings, tailored evals, scoped engineering
  tasks, and targeted plus regression validation. Design use: capture signal → generalize → evaluate
  → change, with practitioner evidence preserved.
- **2026-05-29 — [A shared playbook for trustworthy third-party
  evaluations](https://openai.com/index/trustworthy-third-party-evaluations-foundations/).** Requires
  the tested claim, harness, tools, budget, retries, scoring, limitations, and validity checks to be
  reported. Design use: results from different models, timeouts, or harnesses are not a comparison.
- **2026-06-04 — [Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful
  ChatGPT](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-memory-dreaming/).** Frames memory synthesis around
  correctness, freshness, relevance, and scale. Design use: retained context needs a lifecycle;
  monotonic accumulation is not sufficient.
- **2026-07-08 — [Separating signal from noise in coding
  evaluations](https://openai.com/index/separating-signal-from-noise-coding-evaluations/).** Its
  human-supervised audit estimates roughly 30 percent of SWE-Bench Pro tasks are broken. Design use:
  a failing grader may be the defect, so unexplained failures are diagnosed before they become rules.
- **2026-07-15 — [GPT-Red: Unlocking Self-Improvement for
  Robustness](https://openai.com/index/unlocking-self-improvement-gpt-red/).** Keeps automated
  adversarial discovery as a distinct lane alongside human and third-party red teaming. Design use:
  do not collapse authoring and adversarial evaluation into one context.
- **2026-07-20 — [Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon
  models](https://openai.com/index/safety-alignment-long-horizon-models/).** Reports novel internal
  failures, a pause in access, new trajectory evaluations and monitoring, then limited restoration.
  Design use: continuous operation needs observation, pause, rollback, and staged resumption.

## Recent research and preprints

These results are research evidence, not production guarantees. Reported deltas are meaningful only
under the authors' datasets, models, budgets, and graders.

- **2026-04-02 — [CoEvoSkills: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Co-Evolutionary
  Verification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01687).** Separates a skill generator from a surrogate
  verifier and protects held-out oracle details. Supports separate verification and resistance to
  tuning directly against the answer key.
- **2026-04-03 — [Supply-Chain Poisoning Attacks Against LLM Coding Agent Skill
  Ecosystems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03081).** Tests 1,070 adversarial skills and reports that
  document-embedded payloads can bypass model defenses and sometimes combined static/alignment
  screening. Supports treating every imported or generated skill as untrusted supply-chain input;
  this is a preprint and does not establish the risk rate for this fleet.
- **2026-04-06 — [How Well Do Agentic Skills Work in the
  Wild](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04323).** Finds skill benefits become fragile as retrieval and
  relevance conditions become more realistic across a 34,000-skill corpus, although refinement can
  recover performance in some settings. Supports negative routing tests and measuring skill
  selection, not only force-loaded use.
- **2026-04-09 — [SkillForge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08618).** Separates failure analysis,
  skill diagnosis, and optimization across 1,883 support tickets and 3,737 tasks. Supports explicit
  lifecycle stages instead of a single “reflect and rewrite” prompt.
- **2026-04-22 — [SkillLearnBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.20087).** Provides a benchmark for
  continual skill generation from agent experience. Supports evaluating the learning method, not
  just the final task result.
- **2026-05-18 — [SkillsVote](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18401).** Treats raw trajectories as noisy
  and environment-sensitive, attributes outcomes across skill use, exploration, environment, and
  result signals, then uses evidence-gated updates. Supports provenance and conservative admission.
- **2026-05-22 — [From Raw Experience to Skill
  Consumption](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23899).** Finds model-generated skills beneficial on
  average but with non-trivial negative transfer and model-dependent extractor/consumer behavior.
  Supports consumer-specific regression testing rather than assuming a generally useful lesson.
- **2026-05-25 — [CODESKILL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25430).** Uses rubric feedback plus
  verifiable execution reward against a frozen downstream agent and maintains a stable-size skill
  bank. Supports combined qualitative/executable grading and non-monotonic maintenance.
- **2026-05-26 — [MUSE-Autoskill](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27366).** Models creation, memory,
  management, evaluation, and refinement as one lifecycle with unit-test and runtime feedback.
  Supports explicit lifecycle stages and cross-task evaluation.
- **2026-06-06 — [SKILL.nb](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08049).** Stores versioned auditable
  workflows with execution gates, fallback paths, evidence, bounded repair, and target-version tests.
  Supports applicability/freshness checks and rollback-aware repair.
- **2026-06-06 — [PACE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08106).** Shows that repeatedly keeping any
  positive noisy dev-set delta can accept false and harmful self-modifications; its paired sequential
  test sharply reduces those admissions in the reported experiments. Supports a meaningful-effect
  gate and rejection of “score went up once.”
- **2026-07-01 — [From Registry to Repository](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00911).** Its empirical
  study of 18,463 registry skills and 23,199 personal-use skills reports largely one-time reuse and
  overwhelmingly additive later maintenance. Supports explicit merge, supersede, and drop paths;
  the observation does not prove a particular deduplication algorithm.
- **2026-07-11 — [Dynamic Agent Skills: A Lifecycle Survey and
  Taxonomy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10113).** Synthesizes a 124-paper audit into evidence,
  proposal, verification/admission, storage, retrieval, maintenance, portability, and governance.
  Supports lineage, rollback, supersession, staleness, and pruning as first-class concerns.
- **2026-07 — [SAGE: Reinforcement Learning for Self-Improving Agent with Skill
  Library](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.69/), ACL 2026.** Reports higher AppWorld goal
  completion with fewer steps and tokens for its trained setup. This peer-reviewed positive result
  establishes potential value, not permission for autonomous promotion in a prompt-file fleet.

## Blogs, conferences, and practitioner evidence

- **2026-04-08 — [Feedback
  Flywheel](https://martinfowler.com/articles/reduce-friction-ai/feedback-flywheel.html)** and the
  **2026-04-15 [Thoughtworks Technology Radar
  entry](https://www.thoughtworks.com/en-us/radar/techniques/feedback-flywheel)** route session
  signals into shared artifacts with a human on the loop and warn about context rot/noisy feedback.
  This directly supports a lightweight task scan plus reviewed promotion.
- **2026-04-26/27 — [ICLR 2026 workshops](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2026/events/workshop)** included
  dedicated Lifelong Agents and Recursive Self-Improvement programs covering continual learning,
  evaluation, governance, stability, and safety. This establishes current research attention; a
  workshop agenda is not evidence that any particular mechanism works.
- **2026-05-26 — [Agent Skills '26](https://www.agentskills-workshop.org/), CAIS.** A dedicated
  workshop covered skill design, evaluation, optimization, lifecycle, and security. This establishes
  active practitioner/research focus; the program is ecosystem context rather than efficacy proof.
- **2026-05-16 — [Compound Engineering: How I Ship More by Writing Less
  Code](https://datasciencefestival.com/session/compound-engineering-how-i-ship-more-by-writing-less-code/),
  Data Science Festival.** Presents plan → work → review → compound, specialized review/test agents,
  reusable conventions, and human oversight. Supports artifact routing and review, as practitioner
  experience rather than controlled research.
- **2026-06-01/02 — [QCon AI Boston](https://boston.qcon.ai/schedule/boston2026).** Its program made
  agent evaluation, governance, zero trust, observability, and reusable evaluation frameworks
  first-class production topics. Used as ecosystem context, not a source of quantitative claims.
- **2026-06-29 through 2026-07-02 — [AI Engineer World's Fair
  schedule](https://www.ai.engineer/worldsfair/schedule?view=list).** Included “From Signal to PR:
  Anatomy of a Self-Improving Agent” and production-agent evaluation sessions. Used as current
  practice context; the schedule alone does not validate a method.
- **2026-07-03 — [Self-Improving AI Agents: When Skill Optimization
  Works](https://www.pymc-labs.com/blog-posts/self-improving-ai-agents).** Reports strong wins in
  some task families but roughly one genuine improvement per three optimization runs, one harmful
  edit, large seed variation, and an observed ±0.06 no-change noise floor. Supports multi-seed
  reporting and refusing small apparent gains.
- **2026-07-22 — [Towards Automating Eval
  Engineering](https://www.langchain.com/blog/towards-automating-eval-engineering).** Recommends
  mining repository context and traces, iterating with user approval, inspecting both agent and
  verifier trajectories for reward hacking, and rerunning a stable environment. This corroborates
  the loop operationally but is a vendor practitioner report, not controlled causal evidence.

## OSS implementation evidence

GitHits was used to inspect these public repositories separately from the local workspace.
Repository adoption proves implementability, not benefit to this fleet.

- **[anthropics/skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills)**, inspected commit
  `b29e7cf65e5cb78a5ac33d582270551bc74a14eb`: the installed `skill-creator` skill,
  the installed `skill-creator` skill's `scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py` resource, and the skill's `agents/comparator.md` and
  `agents/analyzer.md` define paired skill/baseline runs, mean and sample variance, time/token
  measures, blind comparison, and evidence-grounded analysis without speculation.
- **[microsoft/SkillOpt](https://github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt)**, inspected commit
  `e7014cd18a18e11e6f6c10b897f7a009960d2e1b`: `README.md`, `skillopt/types.py`,
  `skillopt/optimizer/skill.py`, `skillopt/evaluation/gate.py`, `docs/guide/dl-analogy.md`, and
  `skillopt_sleep/mine.py` define a frozen target, bounded typed mutations, a strict held-out gate,
  and separated train/validation/test data. `tests/test_sleep_engine.py` contains source-level
  reward-hacking/regression cases; this research did not execute that upstream suite.
- **[stanfordnlp/dspy](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy)**, inspected commit
  `c69136b29aca4c00ca6da7667f7b80783188980e`: `dspy/teleprompt/gepa/gepa.py` separates training and
  validation, warns against train-as-validation overfitting, and exposes metric/full-eval budgets
  and stopping callbacks.
- **[Leeroo-AI/kapso](https://github.com/Leeroo-AI/kapso)**,
  `benchmarks/relbench/REVIEW_FINDINGS.md`, inspected snapshot prefix `de5d3ed`: a reviewable working
  log containing run/time, reason, proposed fix, status, approval, corrections, regressions, and
  rejected alternatives.
- **[verygoodplugins/mcp-automem](https://github.com/verygoodplugins/mcp-automem)**, `AGENTS.md`,
  inspected snapshot prefix `946f9e`: atomic high-signal records and update/invalidation when fresh
  repository or user evidence contradicts retained state.

## How the evidence changed this skill

- The old two-question micro-retro became a learning scan plus a full evidence record.
- “Move one lesson left” became inventory → one disposition → one primary destination.
- Runbooks gained an explicit update/create/propose admission boundary; unverified advice cannot
  manufacture operator commands.
- Promotion now freezes the baseline and requires targeted, regression/adverse, fresh-context, and
  exact-generated-artifact checks with rollback.
- Maintenance explicitly merges, supersedes, and drops guidance instead of only adding it.
- Every agent reports a lightweight Learning result; only lifecycle owners load the full skill to
  avoid fleet-wide context bloat and duplicate retros.
- A repository-local candidate ledger now preserves first occurrences, recurrence, rejection, and
  freshness as quarantined data while keeping implementation and approval outside the intake tool.

## Limits and open questions

- Most 2026 papers above are preprints and may change after review or replication.
- Provider guidance describes provider-specific systems; cross-host transfer must be tested locally.
- Benchmarks under-report long-term skill-bank history, rejected changes, and security incidents.
- LLM routing and judging are probabilistic; deterministic graders can also be wrong or incomplete.
- The best recurrence threshold is domain- and risk-dependent. “Twice” is a practical default, not a
  statistically universal law.
- A local prompt contract can require a scan and handoff, but it cannot create a background
  scheduler or structural write boundary. The repository-local ledger adds validated bounded
  storage, not autonomous authority; validators, sandboxes, approvals, and independent review
  remain the enforcing controls.
